findings.statement: Publishing an insertion in place beats rewriting the index for it
findings.detail: in place 139402 ops/s writing 509.8 MB, against rewriting 29112 ops/s writing 944.5 MB (in place vs rewrite: greater 4.788x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 9.2%/4.9%)). Every key is new, which is the case `checkpoint_in_place` declined outright until the directory was double-buffered, and which f27 priced at 4.122x

findings.statement: Room to insert does not cost file size
findings.detail: 52.56 MB with room to insert against 385.21 MB without (rewrite vs in place: greater 7.329x (p=0.0001, rel_iqr 0.0%/0.0%)). The directory is doubled so an insertion can be published with one store, which is about 4 bytes per key on an index that is about 57. Supdb already loses the size axis to LMDB (EXT.6), so this is the axis where the change could pay for its speed twice over

notes: both arms interleaved; the only difference is Options::index_inserts
the seed load and the reopen are untimed: the timed phase is insertion only
